subtype: Friend or teacher noticing the shift [Observer]
passage:
Wednesday night.
Tejas again today. Third time this week he said "those people" with that face, like he'd bitten something rotten. His phone is only one channel now. He skipped cricket and Ravi's birthday. He used to be the one who organised everything.
I wanted to argue. I had facts ready. Instead I asked, "What's been going on with you, really?"
He was quiet, then it came out. The scholarship was cut in June. His father's shop is struggling. He feels like nobody listens to people like him. The channel "at least says it out loud."
I didn't agree with the channel. I just said, "That sounds exhausting. I'm sorry nobody listened."
He actually looked at me.
Later, with his okay, I messaged Mr Rao, the college counsellor. He replied tonight: "Thank you. Tell Tejas my door is open tomorrow at eleven, and you can come with him if he likes."
Zainab

qa.q: What time did Mr Rao offer to meet Tejas?
qa.a: Mr Rao offered to meet Tejas tomorrow at eleven.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling before asking Tejas what was going on?
qa.a: Zainab was worried about Tejas and tempted to argue with facts ready, but chose to ask gently what was really going on.

qa.q: Why did Zainab's choice to ask instead of argue help?
qa.a: Asking what was really going on let Tejas share his pain and kept his trust, which made it possible to involve the counsellor.

qa.q: How might Tejas have felt when Zainab said "I'm sorry nobody listened"?
qa.a: Tejas may have felt seen for the first time in months, which is why he actually looked at Zainab.

grounding: Zainab notices Tejas speaking with contempt, watching one channel and withdrawing, listens to the pain beneath it, and brings in the college counsellor.

passage:
Sonali: did you see what I sent. this is why nothing works in this city. it's THEM
Nandini: I saw. you've sent that channel's clips every day this week
Sonali: because they're the only ones telling the truth
Nandini: can I ask something, not to argue
Sonali: what
Nandini: you used to come to Sunday badminton. and you stopped answering Kiran and Farah
Sonali: they don't get it
Nandini: get what?
Sonali: the internship went to someone's nephew. after I did everything right. everything
Sonali: and then I found these videos and at least someone was angry with me
Nandini: that's so unfair. I didn't know. I'm really sorry
Sonali: ok
Nandini: would you talk to Father Mathew at the youth centre? he helped my brother when he was angry at everything. I can come with you
Sonali: maybe
Sonali: can we get food first
Nandini: yes. 7 at the usual place

qa.a: The internship went to someone's nephew.

qa.q: What does Sonali mean by "at least someone was angry with me"?
qa.a: Sonali felt alone and hurt over the internship, and the channel's anger made that hurt feel shared, which is part of its pull.

qa.q: What did Nandini do well in this chat?
qa.a: Nandini said it was not an argument, asked what was really going on, named the unfairness, and offered to go with Sonali to someone who could help.

qa.q: How might Kiran and Farah have experienced Sonali's silence?
qa.a: They were probably confused and hurt at being dropped, without knowing about the internship behind it.

grounding: Nandini notices Sonali sharing contempt from one channel and cutting off Kiran and Farah, listens to the hurt beneath it and suggests help from a community leader.
